implemented_requirements.requirement: Snake moves based on directional inputs (arrow keys or WASD)
implemented_requirements.evidence: on_key method maps "Up", "Down", "Left", "Right", "w", "a", "s", "d" to direction vectors and updates pending direction.
In tick(), when head position equals self.food the score is increased and the snake tail is not popped, effectively growing the snake.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Food appears at random locations not occupied by snake
implemented_requirements.evidence: spawn_food() builds a list of free cells (excluding self.snake) and selects one with random.choice.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game ends on collision with self
implemented_requirements.evidence: tick() checks if the new head position (nx, ny) is in self.snake[:-1]; if so, game_over() is called.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game ends on collision with boundary
implemented_requirements.evidence: tick() verifies 0 <= nx < COLS and 0 <= ny < ROWS; violation triggers game_over().
render() redraws the canvas each tick; tick() schedules the next call with after(self.speed, self.tick).
status label is updated in render() with "Score: %d  Best: %d" using self.score.
DIFFICULTIES dict defines "Easy", "Medium", "Hard" with different speeds; buttons created in __init__ call start(s) with the selected speed.
When head reaches food, self.score += 1 in tick().

critical_issues: The program depends on the Tkinter GUI library; execution will fail in environments without a display or without Tkinter installed.
judge.summary: The provided main.py implements a functional classic Snake game with directional controls, food spawning, growth, collision detection, score display, and selectable difficulty levels. All core requirements are met, and the code is likely executable in a standard Python environment with Tkinter. Minor risk exists only if the runtime lacks GUI support.
